Trump signed an executive order Friday waiving the application of several duties, sanctions and restrictions under the Graham Act, which he signed last month. The measures included tariffs on Russian goods and penalties on countries buying Russian oil and gas. They were due to take effect next week.
“A lot of you don’t know what my decision is yet, but we’ll figure it out, and you’ll ​figure it out,” Trump told reporters at his Mar-a-Lago club in Florida.
60-Day Review Could Affect Energy Markets
Secretary of State
Marco Rubio
told reporters before boarding a plane for Uzbekistan that Trump could take up to 60 days to assess the economic impact. The order did not specify the waiver’s length.
He said the review will weigh what the measures mean "to the global economy and even to the US economy."

Rubio also defended a separate agreement with Russia to boost diesel supply. Trump said Russia would initially send more than 300,000 metric tons to the United States, with more shipments in November and beyond.
Escalating conflict in the Middle East has disrupted global oil flows, adding to pressure on Trump over high energy prices.
